precepts.text: Thus saith the Lord to his anointed, to Cyrus. Why is that important? This was written, write this down, 150 years before the birth of Cyrus. So when he came of age, he was shown his name in the scriptures, and he knew the God of Israel, based on that prophecy, was dealing with him to release his people.
precepts.point: Verse three: he makes a proclamation to all 12 tribes. Who is there among you of all his people? He's not just talking to Judah. And whosoever remaineth in any place where he sojourneth: if you decide you don't want to go back to the land of Israel, you want to stay where you've been living for all these decades, let the men of his place help him with silver, and with gold, and with goods, and with beasts. So some of the northern kingdom did go back with the kingdom of Judah; some of the southern kingdom decided, no, we're going to stay out here too. Everybody did not go back.

precepts.why:
During the Persian captivity we got liberty. Cyrus proclaimed, “The Lord God of heaven hath given me all the kingdoms of the earth”, and he said that because he knew it was a prophecy. Isaiah had written it: “Thus saith the Lord to his anointed, to Cyrus, whose right hand I have holden, to subdue nations before him; and I will loose the loins of kings, to open before him the two leaved gates; and the gates shall not be shut”.

Why is that important? Write this down: it was written 150 years before the birth of Cyrus. So when he came of age, he was shown his name in the scriptures, and he knew that the God of Israel, based on that prophecy, was dealing with him to release his people. It goes into more detail in the writings of Flavius Josephus, how the prophets showed Cyrus what he must do. And he obeyed.

So he made his proclamation to all twelve tribes: “Who is there among you of all his people?” Not just Judah. And whoever chose to stay where they had been living for decades, “let the men of his place help him with silver, and with gold, and with goods, and with beasts”. Some of the northern kingdom went back with Judah; some of the southern kingdom stayed out. Everybody did not go back.

precepts.text: This is the counsel, and it is Cyrus speaking: who is there among you of all his people? his God be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem, which is in Judah, and build the house of the Lord God of Israel. And whosoever remaineth in any place where he sojourneth, let the men of his place help him with silver, and with gold, and with goods, and with beasts. That was the proclamation charged to Israel.
precepts.point: For through that country there was a great way to go, namely, of a year and a half: and the same region is called Arsareth. A year and a half of travel means stops along the way: the maritime ports. From the book Maritime Trade and the Movement of Culture, by the sister the teacher interviewed on the Quest voyage and whose museum in Charleston the nation plans to visit: the Red Sea and Indian Ocean connected Africa to the wider world as early as the third century BCE, trading gold, ivory, spices, and textiles with Arabia, India, Persia, and China, with cultural diffusion along the coasts.

precepts.why:
Between verse 40 and verse 41 of 2 Esdras 13 there is a whole lot of history. Verse 40 is Assyria: “whom Salmanasar the king of Assyria led away captive”, before Babylon and before the Persians. Then Babylon took down Assyria and took her captives, and moved down and took Judah. Then the Persians came in. None of that is mentioned in the two verses; it jumps from Assyria to Persia, under Cyrus. So when verse 41 says “But they took this counsel among themselves”, what is the counsel? Ezra shows it.

“Who is there among you of all his people? his God be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem, which is in Judah, and build the house of the Lord God of Israel, (he is the God,) which is in Jerusalem.” It is Cyrus speaking: the proclamation between the Most High and him, allowing Israel to go back and build in exchange for being able to take down Babylon.

“And whosoever remaineth in any place where he sojourneth, let the men of his place help him with silver, and with gold, and with goods, and with beasts, beside the freewill offering for the house of God that is in Jerusalem.” That was what was charged to Israel to go and do.

But the counsel the tribes took among themselves was different: “that they would leave the multitude of the heathen, and go forth into a further country, where never mankind dwelt”. The bulk of them said, we are not staying; we are not going back to build in Jerusalem; we are going to a further country. Ezra and Nehemiah are the first two books of Ezra, and 1 Esdras and 2 Esdras are the third and fourth, and together they detail this history.

precepts.text: The Most High stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia in 539 BC, that the word of the Lord by the mouth of Jeremiah might be fulfilled. Who is there among you of all his people? His God be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem and build the house of the Lord God of Israel. Cyrus gave us freedom to go back; the ten tribes instead took counsel to go into a further country.
precepts.point: Book read in class, Lost Tribes and Promised Lands, on the Marrano navigator Montezinos: he heard an exclamation of thanksgiving that blessed God for not making the speaker an idolater, a barbarian, a negro, or an Indian, and it dawned on him: those Indians, they are Hebrews. Later, strangers who came by canoe told him in their common ancestral tongue that they were themselves of the tribe of Reuben, and that the tribe of Joseph lived on an island nearby. Ephraim and Manasseh make up the tribe of Joseph: the islands. They asked him to send twelve bearded men to be their teachers, for though they spoke Hebrew they could not read or write it. The sorcerers of Francisco's tribe had perceived that they were a special people who should be left alone, that the God of these children of Israel is the true God, that everything inscribed on their tablets is true, and that at the end of days they will be lords of all the nations of the earth. Montezinos turned the tale into propaganda for the Dutch conquest of Brazil; Esau turned even this knowledge into conquest.

precepts.why:
“Those are the ten tribes, which were carried away prisoners out of their own land in the time of Osea the king, whom Salmanasar the king of Assyria led away captive”. That was the Assyrian captivity, 722 BC; the northern kingdom was forcefully displaced into Assyria. Then Esdras says, “But they took this counsel among themselves, that they would leave the multitude of the heathen”. That is a jump in history, into the Persian captivity, when Cyrus the Persian gave us freedom.

For our people who don't know that history, Ezra 1 shows it: “Now in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, that the word of the Lord by the mouth of Jeremiah might be fulfilled, the Lord stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia”. The Most High moved the king of Persia in 539 BC. Cyrus proclaimed, “The Lord God of heaven hath given me all the kingdoms of the earth; and he hath charged me to build him an house at Jerusalem, which is in Judah.”

“Who is there among you of all his people? his God be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem”. His people: not Persians, but Israelites, God's people. “And whosoever remaineth in any place where he sojourneth, let the men of his place help him with silver, and with gold, and with goods, and with beasts”. Whether we were in Assyria or in Persia, wherever we were scattered and displaced, we were given freedom to go back to Israel and build the house of God.

That is what 2 Esdras 13 is recording. The ten tribes were given that freedom, but they took counsel to go instead “into a further country, where never mankind dwelt, That they might there keep their statutes, which they never kept in their own land.” The northern kingdom wanted a fresh start, tired of captivity after captivity: Assyrian, Babylonian, Persian. So they went into Arsareth, the land Columbus identified as America. Our land is Israel; we were not always in the islands.

note.label: The Iranians & The Ephesians

precepts.why:
Cyrus the Great founded the Achaemenid Empire, the old Persian kingdom, in 550 BC, and it was an ancient Iranian empire. That makes this very significant for what is going on today. “the Lord stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia”, and Cyrus proclaimed, “The Lord God of heaven hath given me all the kingdoms of the earth; and he hath charged me to build him an house at Jerusalem”.

The Lord was working through King Cyrus. The Lord did speak to him, and he listened. Isaiah had already named him: “That saith of Cyrus, He is my shepherd, and shall perform all my pleasure: even saying to Jerusalem, Thou shalt be built; and to the temple, Thy foundation shall be laid.”

So the word of the Lord by the mouth of Jeremiah was fulfilled through a Persian, an Iranian king, called by God his shepherd, who performed all his pleasure: Jerusalem built again and the foundation of the temple laid.

precepts.why:
Isaiah goes on: “Thus saith the Lord to his anointed, to Cyrus, whose right hand I have holden, to subdue nations before him; and I will loose the loins of kings, to open before him the two leaved gates; and the gates shall not be shut”.

That is why Cyrus could say, “The Lord God of heaven hath given me all the kingdoms of the earth”. The Lord held his right hand and subdued nations before him. The Lord used King Cyrus, who was a Persian, to allow us to go back and build the temple.

Cyrus is also the one who gave that decree. And the kingdom he ruled, Persia and Media, is Iran today, which is why his story is very significant for what is going on now.

precepts.why:
Cyrus's coming was prophesied long before, by name. Isaiah says of the Most High, “That saith of Cyrus, He is my shepherd, and shall perform all my pleasure: even saying to Jerusalem, Thou shalt be built; and to the temple, Thy foundation shall be laid.”

Here it comes to pass. In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, the Lord stirs up his spirit and he makes a proclamation throughout all his kingdom: “The Lord God of heaven hath given me all the kingdoms of the earth; and he hath charged me to build him an house at Jerusalem, which is in Judah.” Cyrus was one of the first kings of Persia, and the Most High named him as His shepherd, the one who would say Jerusalem shall be built and the temple's foundation laid, and used him to give the order to rebuild Jerusalem.

note.label: Ezra 1: Cyrus Stirred Up to Send Israel Home

precepts.why:
Ezra says this happened “that the word of the Lord by the mouth of Jeremiah might be fulfilled”. This is that word: “For thus saith the Lord, That after seventy years be accomplished at Babylon I will visit you, and perform my good word toward you, in causing you to return to this place.”

After seventy years at Babylon the Most High promised to visit His people and bring them back to their place. So in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia He stirred up the spirit of Cyrus, and the proclamation went out through all his kingdom to build Him a house at Jerusalem. The return home was the Most High performing His good word, exactly as Jeremiah had spoken it.

precepts.text: Judah, Benjamin, and Levi were the ones the Most High raised up to return and build the house in Jerusalem, marking the southern kingdom as Aholibah/Jerusalem.
precepts.point: The elder is Aholah and her sister is Aholibah; they were the Most High's and bare sons and daughters. Aholah is Samaria, the northern kingdom, and Aholibah is Jerusalem, the southern kingdom.

note.label: Ezekiel 23: Aholah and Aholibah, the Two Harlot Sisters

precepts.why:
Aholibah is Jerusalem. When the captivity returned, “Then rose up the chief of the fathers of Judah and Benjamin, and the priests, and the Levites, with all them whose spirit God had raised, to go up to build the house of the Lord which is in Jerusalem.”

Judah, Benjamin and Levi were the ones the Most High raised up to return and build the house in Jerusalem. Those tribes are the southern kingdom. So Aholibah, Jerusalem, is the southern kingdom, the sister of Aholah, Samaria, the northern kingdom. Both were the Most High's, both bare sons and daughters, and both committed whoredoms in their youth in Egypt, where their breasts were pressed and the teats of their virginity bruised; Israel was already living loose.

precepts.text: Cyrus king of Persia brought forth by the hand of Mithredath the treasurer the vessels of the house of the Most High that Nebuchadnezzar had carried out of Jerusalem.
precepts.point: Nebuchadnezzar carried those vessels into the land of Shinar to the house of his god and put them in his treasure house. This came to pass exactly as the prophets had warned.

note.label: Daniel 1: The Best of Israel Carried to Babylon

precepts.why:
The vessels Nebuchadnezzar carried into the land of Shinar to the house of his god did not stay there. “Also Cyrus the king brought forth the vessels of the house of the Lord, which Nebuchadnezzar had brought forth out of Jerusalem, and had put them in the house of his gods; Even those did Cyrus king of Persia bring forth by the hand of Mithredath the treasurer, and numbered them unto Sheshbazzar, the prince of Judah.”

Ezra confirms the same vessels, taken out of Jerusalem and put in the house of Nebuchadnezzar's gods, and shows Cyrus king of Persia bringing them forth again by the hand of Mithredath the treasurer, numbered unto Sheshbazzar the prince of Judah.

precepts.text: The chief of the fathers of Judah and Benjamin, and the priests, and the Levites, went up to build the house of the Lord which is in Jerusalem.
precepts.point: The Jews in that day were Judah, Benjamin and Levi, not all twelve tribes. The Samaritans were Ephraim, and the reason for the separation is written in the prophets.

note.label: John 4: The Woman at the Well and the Nobleman's Son

precepts.why:
The woman of Samaria asked, “How is it that thou, being a Jew, askest drink of me, which am a woman of Samaria? for the Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans.” The Jews in that day were Judah, Benjamin and Levi, not all twelve tribes. Ezra shows who went back to Jerusalem: “Then rose up the chief of the fathers of Judah and Benjamin, and the priests, and the Levites, with all them whose spirit God had raised, to go up to build the house of the Lord which is in Jerusalem.”

Judah, Benjamin, and the priests and the Levites: those are the Jews. Christ, being a Jew, was of those tribes. The Samaritans were another people, Ephraim, and the reason for the separation is written in the prophets.
